scenes.tts: What happens to a photoreceptor if you cut its calcium feedback?
scenes.visual: Title card: Cut the Loop. A calcium loop around a rod outer segment, with scissors beside it.
scenes.narration: What happens to a photoreceptor if you cut its calcium feedback?

scenes.tts: Calcium enters through the open channels. An exchanger pumps it out all the time.
scenes.caption: Calcium enters through the open channels. An exchanger pumps it out all the time.
scenes.visual: Outer-segment membrane: calcium ions flowing in through open channels, and an exchanger pumping calcium out. Label: N C K X exchanger.
scenes.narration: Calcium enters through the open channels. An exchanger pumps it out all the time.

scenes.tts: Predict. Light closes the channels, and pumping goes on. Which way does calcium move?
scenes.visual: Channels close under a light flash; the exchanger keeps working. A calcium gauge with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Predict. Light closes the channels, and pumping goes on. Which way does calcium move?

scenes.tts: Calcium falls. Entry drops, while pumping continues.
scenes.visual: The calcium gauge drops. Label: entry falls, extrusion continues.
scenes.narration: Calcium falls. Entry drops, while pumping continues.

scenes.tts: Two main calcium sensors answer. First, the G caps speed c G M P synthesis, up to about twentyfold.
scenes.caption: Two main calcium sensors answer. First, the GCAPs speed cGMP synthesis, up to about twentyfold.
scenes.visual: Arrow one: GCAP1 and GCAP2 to the cyclase, which makes more cGMP. Label: up to about 20-fold.
scenes.narration: Two main calcium sensors answer. First, the GCAPs speed cGMP synthesis, up to about twentyfold.

scenes.tts: More c G M P reopens channels. This is the strongest of the calcium feedbacks.
scenes.caption: More cGMP reopens channels. This is the strongest of the calcium feedbacks.
scenes.visual: The extra cGMP reopens some channels. Label: strongest calcium feedback.
scenes.narration: More cGMP reopens channels. This is the strongest of the calcium feedbacks.

scenes.tts: Second, recoverin lets go of G R K one. That kinase switches off active pigment, so pigment shuts off sooner.
scenes.caption: Second, recoverin lets go of GRK1. That kinase switches off active pigment, so pigment shuts off sooner.
scenes.visual: Arrow two: recoverin releases GRK1; GRK1 switches off an active pigment molecule. Label: pigment off sooner.
scenes.narration: Second, recoverin lets go of GRK1. That kinase switches off active pigment, so pigment shuts off sooner.

scenes.tts: One feedback does two jobs. On a steady background, it reopens channels. That keeps current in reserve.
scenes.visual: The current bar partly refills under a steady background. Label: job one, reserve.
scenes.narration: One feedback does two jobs. On a steady background, it reopens channels. That keeps current in reserve.

scenes.tts: During each new flash, it pushes against the change. Each photon closes less current, for less time.
scenes.visual: A test flash gives a smaller, briefer dip. Label: job two, lower gain.
scenes.narration: During each new flash, it pushes against the change. Each photon closes less current, for less time.

scenes.tts: Now cut the loop. Mendez and colleagues studied mouse rods lacking both G caps.
scenes.caption: Now cut the loop. Mendez and colleagues studied mouse rods lacking both GCAPs.
scenes.visual: The GCAP arrow crossed out. Label: rods lacking GCAP1 and GCAP2; Mendez and colleagues, 2001.
scenes.narration: Now cut the loop. Mendez and colleagues studied mouse rods lacking both GCAPs.

scenes.tts: Predict. In darkness, is a single photon's response bigger or smaller? On a background, does the rod fail sooner or later?
scenes.visual: Two questions on screen: (a) darkness, one photon: bigger or smaller? (b) background: fails at a dimmer or a brighter light?
scenes.narration: Predict. In darkness, is a single photon's response bigger or smaller? On a background, does the rod fail sooner or later?

scenes.tts: In darkness, about five times bigger. Without the G caps, c G M P is restored more slowly, so responses recover far more slowly.
scenes.visual: Single-photon traces: control, small and brief; GCAP-null, about five times larger and much slower. Labels: about 5 times larger; pigment and PDE shutoff still work.
scenes.narration: In darkness, about five times bigger. Without the GCAPs, cGMP is restored more slowly, so responses recover far more slowly.
scenes.caption: In darkness, about five times bigger. Without the GCAPs, cGMP is restored more slowly, so responses recover far more slowly.

scenes.tts: On a background, adaptation was severely compromised.
scenes.visual: Label: adaptation to background light severely compromised (rods).
scenes.narration: On a background, adaptation was severely compromised.

scenes.tts: In cones lacking the G caps and recoverin, the fitted half-sensitivity point sat at about a quarter of normal. That shift was not statistically significant.
scenes.caption: In cones lacking the GCAPs and recoverin, the fitted half-sensitivity point sat at about a quarter of normal. That shift was not statistically significant.
scenes.visual: Two cone fits on one log-log plot, x-axis in photons per µm² per s. Half-sensitivity points marked: control at 48,800; deficient at 12,100. Label: about a quarter (fitted values; shift not significant). Vinberg and Kefalov, 2018.
scenes.narration: In cones lacking the GCAPs and recoverin, the fitted half-sensitivity point sat at about a quarter of normal. That shift was not statistically significant.

scenes.tts: But their sensitivity fell more steeply as the background brightened, and that difference was significant.
scenes.visual: Slopes labelled on the two curves: control n = 1.0; deficient n = 1.5 (significant).
scenes.narration: But their sensitivity fell more steeply as the background brightened, and that difference was significant.

scenes.tts: So removing the feedback makes rod responses larger in the dark, and adaptation worse on a background.
scenes.visual: Table with cell types labelled. Rods lacking GCAPs: about 5 times larger, slow single-photon response; adaptation severely compromised. Cones lacking GCAPs and recoverin: steeper fitted sensitivity decline. Normal: Weber-like over a range of bright backgrounds.
scenes.narration: So removing the feedback makes rod responses larger in the dark, and adaptation worse on a background.

scenes.tts: In darkness, only the trimming of each response can show. On a background, the reserve comes into play too.
scenes.visual: The table rows highlighted in turn: darkness column, then background column.
scenes.narration: In darkness, only the trimming of each response can show. On a background, the reserve comes into play too.

scenes.tts: Now the arithmetic. Take a small, brief test flash of fixed duration. Its extra intensity is contrast times background, and its photon count is that times the duration. Its peak response is about sensitivity times that photon count.
scenes.visual: On screen: small-flash regime; brief flash of fixed duration T. Extra intensity ΔI = C × I; flash photons F = C × I × T; peak response ≈ S(I) × C × I × T. With C and T fixed, the peak response tracks S(I) × I.
scenes.narration: Now the arithmetic. Take a small, brief test flash of fixed duration. Its extra intensity is contrast times background, and its photon count is that times the duration. Its peak response is about sensitivity times that photon count.

scenes.tts: Multiply sensitivity by background. For normal cones, the product climbs to a ceiling. On bright backgrounds, contrast responses hold.
scenes.visual: Table titled Illustrative fit calculations, units photons per µm² per s. Control cones, (S/Sdark) × I: 24,400 at 48,800; 46,500 at 10^6; 48,600 at 10^7. Rows 10^6 and 10^7 marked: beyond tested range (tested up to about 400,000). A curve rising toward a ceiling of 48,800.
scenes.narration: Multiply sensitivity by background. For normal cones, the product climbs to a ceiling. On bright backgrounds, contrast responses hold.

scenes.tts: For the knockout-cone fit, well above the half-sensitivity background, the product falls about threefold for each tenfold brightening.
scenes.visual: Deficient cones, (S/Sdark) × I: about 5,400 at 48,800; 1,330 at 10^6; 420 at 10^7, with the same extrapolation marks: the two brightest rows are extrapolations of the fitted equation. A falling line.
scenes.narration: For the knockout-cone fit, well above the half-sensitivity background, the product falls about threefold for each tenfold brightening.

scenes.tts: A fall steeper than Weber's rule fits a cell running short of current. But the slope alone cannot measure the current.
scenes.visual: The falling deficient curve highlighted. Label: consistent with less current in reserve; the slope is not a current measurement.
scenes.narration: A fall steeper than Weber's rule fits a cell running short of current. But the slope alone cannot measure the current.

scenes.tts: Some adaptation survives the cut. What supplies it is still unresolved.
scenes.visual: A dashed box with a question mark: some adaptation remains; cause unresolved.
scenes.narration: Some adaptation survives the cut. What supplies it is still unresolved.

scenes.tts: Rods in bright light raise the same question. On a very bright background, mouse rod-driven responses dip at first.
scenes.visual: A contrast-sensitivity trace from rod-driven ganglion cells in cone-deficient mice: a drop soon after a bright background comes on.
scenes.narration: Rods in bright light raise the same question. On a very bright background, mouse rod-driven responses dip at first.

scenes.tts: Then they recover with continued exposure. A model suggests that gain changes and pigment bleaching help.
scenes.visual: The trace climbs back over time. Labels: gain changes; bleaching. Tikidji-Hamburyan and colleagues, 2017.
scenes.narration: Then they recover with continued exposure. A model suggests that gain changes and pigment bleaching help.

scenes.tts: So in these mice, rods do not simply switch off in bright light.
scenes.visual: A rod icon still active under a sun icon. Label: mouse retina and thalamus.
scenes.narration: So in these mice, rods do not simply switch off in bright light.

scenes.tts: The takeaway. The feedback trims each response and keeps current in reserve. Cut it, and the cell runs short sooner.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: a loop with two outputs, trims each response and keeps current in reserve; a cut loop beside a lower current bar and a small dashed box: some adaptation remains.
scenes.narration: The takeaway. The feedback trims each response and keeps current in reserve. Cut it, and the cell runs short sooner.
